title: Genesis 39:19–23
context: Potiphar’s anger sends Joseph to the king’s prison. The LORD is with him there too: steadfast love, favor with the keeper, charge of the prisoners, and success the LORD makes.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: What older interpreters in each camp said about prison, steadfast love, and the LORD making Joseph prosper.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: God despiseth not his prisoners, Psa 69:33. No gates nor bars can shut out his gracious presence from his people. God gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison—God can raise up friends for his people even where they little expect them.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the Old Testament (on Gen 39:21)

reformed.quote: It appears, from the testimony of the Psalmist just cited, that Joseph's extreme sufferings were not immediately alleviated. The Lord purposely suffered him to be reduced to extremity, that he might bring him back as from the grave. We know that as the light of the sun is most clearly seen when we are looking from a dark place; so, in the darkness of our miseries, the grace of God shines more brightly when, beyond expectation, he succors us.

verses.text: When his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his wrath was kindled.
verses.arminianNotes: He hears her words; anger kindles. No cross-examination is recorded. Masters remain accountable for rage that skips the truth. Joseph’s integrity does not control Potiphar’s verdict.
verses.reformedNotes: Anger kindled by a lie still moves the story God is writing. Potiphar’s wrath is grave and unjust; it is not outside providence. The next room is a prison the LORD already occupies.

verses.text: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
verses.arminianNotes: Taken, put, confined: he was there. Here the innocent suffers. Classical Arminians refuse to call the injustice good. Joseph must now live faithfully in a place he did not earn.
verses.reformedNotes: The king’s prison is not a random hole. Reformed readers already see cupbearer and baker on this hallway. “He was there” is location under the God who was with him in the house.

verses.text: But the LORD was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
verses.arminianNotes: The same refrain, now in a cell: the LORD was with Joseph. Steadfast love and favor are given. Arminians hear mercy that does not wait for release. You can receive God’s hesed inside a wrong sentence.
verses.reformedNotes: Hesed in prison is covenant love, not a mood. Presence is not proved by promotion only. The LORD gives favor with the keeper as surely as He gave it with Potiphar.
verses.keyContrast: Both cling to “the LORD was with Joseph” in prison. Arminians stress mercy sincerely given in suffering, to be received by faith; Calvinists emphasize sovereign hesed that does not leave the man God is sending toward Egypt’s throne.

verses.text: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.
verses.arminianNotes: Joseph is again put in charge of everything. Trust repeats in a harder house. Faithfulness in the small overseeing is still required. Presence does not nullify the work.
verses.reformedNotes: The pattern of verses 4–6 returns behind bars. God is rehearsing Joseph’s future administration. Whatever was done there passed through the hands the LORD was training.

verses.text: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because the LORD was with him; and that which he did, the LORD made it prosper.
verses.arminianNotes: The keeper’s ease has the same cause as Potiphar’s: the LORD was with him. Arminians end where the chapter began—success as the LORD’s doing, and Joseph still doing the work. Prison has not expelled God.
verses.reformedNotes: Inclusio: the LORD made it prosper. House and dungeon rhyme because God has not changed. The path from pit to prison is still the path of the God who will keep His promise to Abraham through this man.
